questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Study the algorithm below and answer the questions that follow.

1. Start
2. Get marks for test 1 and test 2: Mark 1, Mark 2
3. If either Mark 1 is less than zero OR Mark 2 is less than zero
4. Display "Mark cannot be negative"
5. Else
6. Average mark = (Mark 1 + Mark 2)/2
7. Display Mark 1, Mark 2, Average mark
8. End

(i) Define the term algorithm. (2 marks)

(ii) Copy and complete the table below by carrying out a dry run of the above algorithm. (2 marks)

| Mark 1 | Mark 2 | Display |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 10 | |
| -20 | 15 | |

(iii) Represent the above algorithm using a flowchart. (5 marks)

(iv) Locate by stating the line numbers of any one control structure used in the algorithm. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Algorithm (2 marks).** An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of clear step-by-step instructions that solves a problem or carries out a task. It does not depend on any programming language.

**(ii) Dry run (2 marks, 1 mark per row)**

Row 1: Mark 1 = 14 and Mark 2 = 10, neither is less than zero, so the Else part runs: Average mark = (14 + 10)/2 = 24/2 = 12.

Row 2: Mark 1 = -20 is less than zero, so the condition is true and line 4 runs. Lines 6 and 7 are skipped.

| Mark 1 | Mark 2 | Display |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 10 | 14, 10, 12 |
| -20 | 15 | Mark cannot be negative |

**(iii) Flowchart (5 marks)**

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_5_fig_1.png)

Marking points: Start and End terminal symbols (1); input symbol "Get Mark 1 and Mark 2" (1); decision "Mark 1 < 0 OR Mark 2 < 0" with a Yes branch and a No branch (2); correct actions on each branch: display the message on Yes, calculate and display the three values on No, both branches joining at End (1).

**(iv) Control structure (2 marks).** The algorithm uses **selection** (an IF ... ELSE structure): it starts at line 3 (If) and includes line 4 (action if true), line 5 (Else) and lines 6 and 7 (actions if false). Lines 1, 2 and 8 are executed one after the other in a simple **sequence** (also accepted as a control structure).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Briefly explain the difference between,

(i) An algorithm and a program code. (2 marks)

(ii) A compiler and an interpreter. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Algorithm and program code (2 marks).** An algorithm is the plan of the solution: a list of steps written in plain language, in pseudocode or as a flowchart, independent of any programming language, which a person reads. A program code is the implementation of that algorithm in a particular programming language (for example Pascal, C or Python) with its strict syntax, which the computer can run once it has been translated into machine code.

**(ii) Compiler and interpreter (2 marks).** Both translate a program written in a high-level language into machine language. A **compiler** translates the whole program at once, produces a separate executable file and then reports all the errors; the program runs quickly afterwards and the source code is not needed to run it. An **interpreter** translates and executes the program one statement at a time, stops at the first error, produces no executable file and has to translate the program again each time it is run, so it runs more slowly.
